7 May 1572 [O.S.]Johannes Pratensis → Tycho BraheResponds with playful alchemical and Neoplatonic imagery to praise the extemporaneous quality of Tycho's writing, comparing its heat to solar and divine inspiration.text
17 May 1572 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Johannes PratensisReplies in hendecasyllabic verse cast as prose, expressing delight at Pratensis's letter and lamenting the displacement of true learning by scholastic barbarism.text
16 April 1573 [O.S.]Johannes Pratensis → Tycho BraheReports on the gilding of Tycho's celestial globe — the goldsmith cannot lay gold stars on silver, the painter would smother the engraving — and urges an all-gold scheme with matt figures on a burnished ground, costed at four rose nobles; then on the printing of De nova stella, arguing Tycho out of the title-word Lucubrationes.text
1 July 1573 [O.S.]Johannes Major → Tycho BraheSends a kinsman with greetings and solicits Tycho's opinion on the new star of 1572, noting sharp disagreement among learned men over its nature.text
10 March 1574 [O.S.]Paul Hainzel → Tycho BraheReports observations of the 1572 Cassiopeia star made with the Augsburg quadrant, finding zero parallax and therefore a supralunary position, despite reluctance to contradict Aristotle.text
7 March 1575 [O.S.]Hieronymus Wolf → Tycho BraheReports that a carrier's treachery caused Tycho to miss acquiring Ambrosius's library and Schreckenfuchs's armilla, and offers to help procure the latter.text
11 March 1575 [O.S.]Paul Hainzel → Tycho BraheReports that Schreckenfuchs's Ptolemaic armillae have been obtained and will be sent with Regiomontanus's treatise on the instrument's construction and use.text
31 January 1576 [O.S.]Johannes Pratensis → Tycho BraheConfirms forwarding a sealed box and money to Rostock and expresses eagerness to hear Tycho's news from his recent travels through Germany.text
14 February 1576 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Johannes PratensisConfirms the Rostock business was handled and reveals a secret plan to depart for Germany, asking Pratensis to share it only with the French Ambassador Dançay.text
15 February 1576 [O.S.]Johannes Pratensis → Tycho BraheExpresses joy at the king's gracious invitation for Tycho to remain in Denmark, interpreting it as divine providence, and urges Tycho to accept.text
14 May 1576 [O.S.]Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheReturns borrowed Greek propositions, mentions forwarding a sundials manuscript, and approves Tycho's resolve to devote himself to celestial observations.text
2 August 1576 [O.S.]Johannes Major → Tycho BraheThanks Tycho for the gift of his book on the New Star, congratulates him on safe return to his homeland, and expresses continued regard.text
23 August 1576 [O.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheRecalls their meeting at Regensburg and expresses grief at their swift parting, explaining the long delay in writing by lawsuits and pressing occupations.text
21 November 1576 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Joachim CamerariusAsks Camerarius to collect the remaining books from Brechtel's dispersed library and add any mathematics or chemical titles found, to be shipped via Georg Labenwolf.text
8 December 1576 [O.S.]Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheReplies to Tycho's remarks on wasted clear skies and discusses the obstacles to astronomy from foul weather and academic neglect of the subject.text
20 September 1577 [O.S.]Johannes Major → Tycho BraheReports a prior letter of thanks for Tycho's treatise on the 1572 star, and describes discussions with Schissler and Gemperlin regarding the construction of a globe.text
9 May 1578 [O.S.]Hieronymus Wolf → Tycho BraheNotes Tycho's failure to write after Gemperlinus's return from Denmark, and reflects on the astrological prediction of danger to life Tycho had made for him.text
4 December 1578 [O.S.]Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheReports finding Maestlin's book on the 1577 comet in the Frankfurt catalogue and offers to forward it, discussing whether Tycho's own demonstration should supersede refutation of others.text
1579 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Hieronymus WolfReports receiving German comet writings via Paul Hainzel, praises Maestlin's observations and demonstration above the rest, and discusses solar apogee, eccentricity, and the eighth sphere.text
25 March 1579 [O.S.]Paul Hainzel → Tycho BraheExcuses his infrequent letters due to difficulty in Latin, reports his household in good health, and notes the birth of a son in September 1577.text
25 March 1579 [O.S.]Hieronymus Wolf → Tycho BraheWrites briefly due to the courier's haste, reports inability to procure German comet writings, and comments on Danish language and the history of the Cimbri and Teutons.text
21 May 1579 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Anders Sørensen VedelDiscusses arrangements regarding a horse offered by Master Franciscus and addresses an unnamed adversary's refusal of reconciliation, deferring judgment to the arriving Legate.text
5 July 1579 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Anders Sørensen VedelInvites Vedel and the Lord Legate to visit Hven, urging that Laurentius, Doctor Franciscus, Master Ezoccus, and the Royal Treasurer also accompany them.text
15 August 1579 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Anders Sørensen VedelReports writing to Machabæus about horses and encloses letters of introduction to Camerarius, Hainzel, and Wolf in Nuremberg and Augsburg for Vedel's forthcoming journey.text
8 February 1580 [O.S.]Hieronymus Wolf → Tycho BraheReports his health, criticises German astrologers for errors in predicting the recent eclipse, and urges Tycho's accurate observations to settle the disputed true motion of the Sun.text
14 March 1580 [O.S.]Hieronymus Wolf → Tycho BraheAccompanies two Danish students with a letter of introduction and notes that local astrologers erred in observing a recent eclipse, expecting more exact results from Tycho.text
4 November 1580 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusApologises for the long silence, citing lack of letter-carriers, and introduces Paul Wittich, who has just delivered Hagecius's latest letter.text
12 October 1581 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusSuspects earlier letters went astray, notes receipt of Hagecius's comet booklet brought by Bartholomaeus Scultetus, and prepares to offer the requested opinion on it.text
1 May 1582 [O.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheReports receiving Tycho's letter, regrets his own was not delivered, and defends Wittich, who conveyed Tycho's letter faithfully and invited Hagecius to join him on Hven.text
23 September 1582 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusAcknowledges receipt of Hagecius's letter via a Görlitz merchant, clears Wittich of suspicion, and sends a brief reply despite pressure of affairs and a royal summons.text
1584Tycho Brahe → Heinrich BrucaeusDisapproves of Brucaeus's neglect of mathematical studies, praises his plan to expound Proclus's Hypotheses, and requests a copy, while noting those Hypotheses rest on imperfect Ptolemaic foundations.text
16 February 1584 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Anders Sørensen VedelDeclines the Holstein typographer Vedel proposed, reports engaging another printer and ordering type at the Frankfurt Fair to establish a press at Uraniborg.text
8 June 1584 [O.S.]Johannes Major → Tycho BraheReports procuring books as requested, including Scaliger's work on the Gregorian calendar, and expresses relief at learning Tycho is still alive after rumours of his death.text
12 June 1584 [O.S.]Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheReports forwarding money to Tycho's printer via a carter and discusses solar and lunar motion, noting that Peurbach's calculations outperform Copernicus's in eclipse timings.text
15 July 1584 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Johannes MajorAcknowledges books received, declines the Wellerian ones, and argues that Lutheran theologians had no grounds to incite popular unrest over the Gregorian calendar reform.text
10 December 1584 [O.S.]Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheReports the Frankfurt bookseller brought none of the requested books, provides information on printing types available from Myliander, and notes Clavius's Gnomonice was sold to Rantzau.text
1585Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheSends paper and printing type obtained from Wittenberg, giving prices and delivery details, and notes the carter will bring remaining type once cast.text
8 January 1585 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Henrik RantzauReports the recent visit of Gerhard Rantzau to Uraniborg, praises his talents and character, and describes showing him the astronomical instruments and the new printing house.text
4 April 1585 [O.S.]Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheReports sending the type and books, and remonstrates against Tycho permitting a commonplace almanac with weather predictions to be published at his press.text
18 May 1585 [O.S.]Christoph Rothmann → Tycho BraheReports that Landgrave Wilhelm IV received Tycho's letter and comet treatise with great pleasure, that the Prince will write separately, and begins his own response on astronomical matters.text
23 June 1585 [O.S.]Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheAcknowledges receipt of payment, questions whether Tycho still intends to publish a calendar, and expresses skepticism that astrological prediction can be made reliable.text
25 August 1585 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusThanks Hagecius for the kindness shown to his brother Steno Brahe during the latter's embassy to the Emperor, and pledges to repay the favour.text
20 October 1585 [O.S.]Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Henrik RantzauReports improvements to the Kassel instruments following Paul Wittich's instruction, now achieving quarter-minute precision, and describes a new horizontal quadrant and sextant.text
11 November 1585 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Anders Sørensen VedelReports the dismissal of a servant who committed theft and fornication with a maidservant, and asks Vedel's assistance in the resulting domestic matter.text
13 December 1585 [O.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheSends greetings via a chance messenger — a servant of the Navarrese ambassador passing through Prague — and notes the difficulty of correspondence across such distance.text
1 March 1586 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselResponds to a copy of Wilhelm's letter to Heinrich Rantzau, expressing delight that the Landgrave continues to pursue astronomical studies at a mature age.text
15 March 1586 [O.S.]Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheReports hearing a (false) rumour of Tycho's death, announces the purchase of Clavius's Gnomonice and Magini's Tables with Ephemerides on his behalf, and asks confirmation.text
23 March 1586 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Henrik RantzauExcuses a delayed reply by winter ice blocking the island, and reports having already sent Wilhelm IV a compendious description of the comet observations.text
14 April 1586 [O.S.]Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Tycho BraheThanks Tycho for the comet observations and reports that the Kassel mathematician's observations agree closely with Tycho's after equation of times and longitudes.text
9 May 1586 [O.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheExplains the mutual delay: Tycho's August letter arrived only in March, and Hagecius's lucubrations were returned from Frankfurt after the Navarrese ambassador changed his route.text
1 July 1586 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusAcknowledges simultaneous receipt of two letters, Hagecius's revised Dialexis, and the Imperial printing privilege, and discusses the contents of these items.text
26 August 1586 [O.S.]Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Tycho BraheFollows up on his unanswered April letter, notes that comet and nova-near-Cassiopeia observations agree closely, and requests Tycho's judgment on the Kassel observations.text
7 September 1586 [N.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheAsks Tycho to confirm receipt of earlier letters and Werner's book, and notes that Jacobus Curtius, Vice-Chancellor of the Empire, eagerly awaits Tycho's first publication.text
7 September 1586 [O.S.]Christoph Rothmann → Tycho BraheAsks why Tycho has not replied to letters sent via the Frankfurt fair and conveys the Landgrave's repeated inquiries about the delayed answer.text
14 October 1586 [O.S.]Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Tycho BraheReminds Tycho of two unanswered letters, renewing the request to send his observations of the fixed stars for comparison with Kassel's own.text
1 January 1587 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselApologizes for the long delay in replying, attributing it to distance and infrequent mail opportunities, and begins addressing the Landgrave's astronomical inquiries.text
17 January 1587 [O.S.]Henrik Rantzau → Tycho BrahePraises the correspondence between Tycho and the Landgrave as beneficial to astronomy and congratulates the age for producing princes devoted to the study of the science.text
20 January 1587 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Christoph RothmannAcknowledges Rothmann's April letter with its recondite astronomical discussions, explains the delay in replying, and reports having communicated celestial observations to the Landgrave.text
25 January 1587 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusReturns Hagecius's manuscript on the new star and comets via the Frankfurt fair and advises him to revise his treatment of the 1577 comet before publishing.text
22 May 1587 [O.S.]Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheIntroduces a young scholar visiting Tycho, urges completion of the star catalogue's longitudes and latitudes, and endorses Tycho's dissent from prior authorities if experience warrants it.text
12 August 1587 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Christoph RothmannReports that a messenger returned from Frankfurt with no letters, explaining that the Landgrave had been occupied with a wedding and has promised a reply by courier shortly.text
11 September 1587 [O.S.]Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Tycho BraheThanks Tycho for his observations and reports close agreement with Kassel's in distances and declinations to fractions of a minute, though a five-minute discrepancy in longitudes remains.text
11 October 1587 [O.S.]Christoph Rothmann → Tycho BraheApologizes for the delayed reply, acknowledges Tycho's parallax argument for the comet, but reports his own observations cannot detect parallax, engaging Copernican hypotheses on the point.text
19 October 1587 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Henrik RantzauApologizes for summer silence, explaining he awaited the Landgrave's reply before forwarding copies of their astronomical correspondence, which he now encloses.text
28 October 1587 [O.S.]Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheThanks Tycho for copies of the Hven–Kassel correspondence and engages the evidence for stellar latitude changes linked to variation in the obliquity of the ecliptic.text
14 November 1587 [O.S.]Christoph Rothmann → Tycho BraheCorrects a misquotation in his previous letter: the writers on optics place the dense atmosphere's upper limit not at one terrestrial semidiameter but at a much smaller fraction.text
3 May 1588 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusConfirms Hagecius's manuscript was sent to Frankfurt, advises him to revise his treatment of the 1577 comet, and sends the second volume of his own work on it.text
11 June 1588 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Christoph RothmannExcuses a delayed reply on grounds of illness and pressing occupations, and reports ongoing Venus observations intended to settle a five-minute longitude discrepancy between their star positions.text
16 August 1588 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselExplains a delayed reply by missed courier opportunities and ongoing Venus observations, which he intends to compare with prior morning observations before writing more fully.text
17 August 1588 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusNotes the second book of De mundi aetherei was sent in May, and urges a frank written opinion of its contents before winter cuts off correspondence.text
17 August 1588 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Christoph RothmannExcuses a late reply and, having already sent the second book of De mundi aetherei via Gellius Sascerides, asks for Rothmann's frank opinion of its contents.text
13 September 1588 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Henrik RantzauThanks Rantzau for procuring printing paper and for the chapel engraving honouring the late King, and sends the promised horizontal sundial, delayed because Gerhard Rantzau departed without visiting.text
13 September 1588 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Caspar PeucerOpens a correspondence via Rantzau's introduction and undertakes to address Peucer's doubts about the diagram of Tycho's new world-system hypothesis conveyed through Rantzau.text
20 September 1588 [O.S.]Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheReports forwarding a letter to Bording and the type-founder's refusal to cross to Denmark, and praises the first part of the comet-of-1577 book.text
13 October 1588 [O.S.]Christoph Rothmann → Tycho BraheAcknowledges both recent letters and the second tome of De mundi aetherei, then argues persistently that the celestial matter is elemental air and not aether.text
1 November 1588 [O.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheReports two earlier letters apparently lost, confirms receipt of the book in late July with expressions of delight, and regrets that advancing age limits fuller engagement.text
4 November 1588 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Heinrich BrucaeusForgives a summer silence and responds to Brucaeus's comments on the second Aetherial Phenomena book, welcoming his approval of the earlier sections and of the new hypothesis.text
21 December 1588 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Henrik RantzauConfirms receipt of the sundial, letters, and celestial-hypothesis instrument, then gives instructions for setting the sundial's meridian line by compass and solar observations.text
1589 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Heinrich BrucaeusQuestions whether Brucaeus, despite his stated practice of pressing hard on disputed points before assenting, truly avoids prejudice in weighing opinions, citing evidence from earlier conversations.text
21 February 1589 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselResumes the astronomical correspondence despite receiving no reply, understanding that preparations for a daughter's marriage occupied Wilhelm, and noting that Rothmann had written on the Landgrave's behalf.text
21 February 1589 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Christoph RothmannExcuses a delayed reply to Rothmann's most recent letter and engages with his persistent argument that the celestial matter is elemental air, finding his evasions unconvincing.text
22 March 1589 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusUses Tage Krabbe's departure for Prague as a courier opportunity to press Hagecius once more for a still-awaited reply and further conference.text
23 March 1589 [O.S.]Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheObjects that Tycho's reply lacked expected candour and misread his words, and defends his stated practice of pressing hard on disputed points before assenting.text
10 May 1589 [N.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheReports that a previous letter and Werner's book, sent via Mylius at Görlitz, failed to reach Tycho, and explains the transmission arrangements made.text
10 May 1589 [O.S.]Caspar Peucer → Tycho BraheAcknowledges Tycho's letter and the Tycho–Landgrave Wilhelm comparative observations, delayed four months in transit, and replies via Duke John of Holstein as a courier.text
20 May 1589 [N.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheReports missing Tycho's courier to the Emperor and failing to obtain the book by Io. Francus from the Frankfurt fair booksellers for dispatch.text
26 July 1589 [O.S.]Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Christoph RothmannInstructs Rothmann to write to Tycho via Nicodemus Frischlin, travelling to Denmark, asking what Tycho has in hand and when his earlier work will appear.text
6 August 1589 [O.S.]Christoph Rothmann → Tycho BraheReports that no reply from Tycho arrived at the Frankfurt fair, explains the Landgrave's pressing concern, and notes Frischlin has arrived with a letter from the Prince.text
22 August 1589 [O.S.]Christoph Rothmann → Tycho BraheDefends his previous letter against Tycho's misreading, denying he detracted from Scripture's authority, and cites Augustine as a precedent for speaking freely on sacred texts.text
1 November 1589 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusAcknowledges four letters from Hagecius received over the summer, detailing each one's dispatch and arrival dates and noting the constant delays in transmission.text
20 November 1589 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Anders Sørensen VedelRequests Vedel's overdue draft of the Danish Privilege for the first volume now at press, and asks help finding a papermaker for the newly ready mill.text
24 November 1589 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Christoph RothmannClarifies that his previous letter accused Rothmann not of impiety but only of misapplying Moses's description of the Moon as 'lesser light' to questions of physical magnitude.text
30 November 1589 [O.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheReports approaching the royal legate Vinshemius for a letter from Tycho but finding none, and protests that he has always answered Tycho's letters.text
1590Tycho Brahe → Caspar PeucerExplains the delay in replying: Bongars, a French envoy who delivered Peucer's second letter in Copenhagen, departed for Germany before Tycho could send a reply.text
1590Christoph Rothmann → Henrik RantzauAsks Rantzau to remind Tycho that letters sent the previous September — one from the Landgrave and two from Rothmann on astronomical matters — still await a reply.text
25 January 1590 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusReassures Hagecius that his earlier letters arrived, explains the missed chance to write via Winshemius, and notes fewer visits to court since King Frederick's death.text
23 February 1590 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusSends a letter via the approaching Frankfurt fair, with little new substance to report but unwilling to let the occasion pass without writing.text
23 February 1590 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Christoph RothmannChides Rothmann for slow replies and reports that printing of his first volume is nearly finished, with the third and final part now in press.text
1 April 1590 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselReports a new, pale comet now visible and sends observations, citing the Landgrave's known interest in such phenomena from the comet of five years before.text
2 April 1590 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Henrik RantzauApologizes for delay, reports the inquiry into the Stures' arms via his sister Sophia and Lady Gørvel still unsatisfied, and promises to write when resolved.text
18 April 1590 [O.S.]Christoph Rothmann → Tycho BraheExcuses his delayed reply by describing two years of severe illness — gout and kidney stones — which so weakened him that he could barely trace a letter.text
1 May 1590 [N.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheAcknowledges receipt of three letters including the Apologia, promises a full reply via courier Curtius, and requests specimen models of the sextant and armillae.text
15 May 1590 [O.S.]Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Tycho BraheExplains his silence by Rothmann's illness and his own advancing age, lamenting that mathematical studies he once pursued eagerly are now barely comprehensible to him.text
11 June 1590 [N.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BrahePraises Tycho's letter for its warm recollection of their friendship and learned astronomical disquisition, which he found entirely welcome rather than over-long.text
3 August 1590 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusReports receipt of the new Imperial Privilege via Prague courier, thanks Hagecius for moving Curtius to obtain it, and notes a lost transcript of the Gallican privilege.text
11 September 1590 [N.S.]Giovanni Antonio Magini → Tycho BraheThanks Tycho for sending his book via a Danish student, notes the rarity of Danish publications in Italy, and welcomes the ensuing opportunity for scholarly exchange.text
1 October 1590 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselReports Rothmann's arrival at Uraniborg with Wilhelm's letter and acknowledges the reasons given for the long interruption in correspondence.text
5 October 1590 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Anders Sørensen VedelChides Vedel for long silence, reports the press stands idle for lack of paper, and asks help finding a skilled papermaker for the new Uraniborg mill.text
21 October 1590 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Joachim CamerariusWelcomes news that the second book of the Phaenomenon did not displease Camerarius and that it has been forwarded to Vincenzo Pinelli at Padua.text
1 December 1590 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Giovanni Antonio MaginiAcknowledges Magini's receipt of the second book of De mundi aetherei recentioribus phaenomenis through Gellius Sascerides and notes the letter from Bologna, received 24 November.text
7 December 1590 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Henrik RantzauPresses Rantzau for help procuring a papermaker needed to resume printing at Uraniborg, naming specifically a Caspar who may be working at Rantzau's mill.text
1591 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusAcknowledges Hagecius's acceptance of Tycho's replies to his astronomical objections and praises his candor in conceding rather than defending untenable positions.text
3 February 1591 [O.S.]Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Tycho BraheAsks Tycho to write about conditions in Denmark and to share fixed-star observations for comparison with Kassel's, and mentions a reported unusual animal.text
9 February 1591 [O.S.]Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Christoph RothmannAcknowledges Rothmann's report of prolonged illness and the sketch of Tycho's observatory, wishes him recovery, and cautions that the ailments should not be self-inflicted by excess.text
1 April 1591 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Christoph RothmannDefends himself against Wilhelm's complaint of sparse correspondence by noting that earlier letters with comet observations were apparently never received, as Rothmann was also unaware of them.text
22 May 1591 [O.S.]Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Tycho BraheWelcomes news that the first volume of De recentioribus coeli Phaenomenis is in press, noting particular interest in the fixed-star content, and inquires about Rothmann's welfare.text
1 August 1591 [N.S.]Giovanni Antonio Magini → Tycho BraheReports that the requested Padua observations of the pole and stellar meridian altitudes remain unconducted due to unsuitable conditions, and announces a dedicated work shortly to be sent.text
29 August 1591 [N.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheConcedes complete defeat in the astronomical disputation with Tycho, reports distributing copies of Tycho's portrait among friends including Curtius who forwarded one to Bavaria.text
31 August 1591 [O.S.]Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Tycho BraheRequests the elk Tycho promised, wanting it as a companion for his deer-park elk, and offers Zapfenburger wine in return.text
8 September 1591 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselExplains the three-and-a-half-month delay in receiving Wilhelm's May letter, then discusses the first volume of De Recentioribus coeli Phaenomenis and its treatment of the stellar restoration.text
26 September 1591 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselReports that the promised elk broke its leg and died before it could be sent, and notes that a prior letter explaining this was dispatched via Henrik Ramel.text
1 February 1592 [N.S.]Giovanni Antonio Magini → Tycho BraheAnnounces the discovery of a quick method for extracting square roots of large numbers after years of effort, and previews the result for Tycho before wider publication.text
20 February 1592 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselReports that elk are on order from Norway but winter has delayed shipping, promises to inform Wilhelm when animals are ready for collection in spring, and mentions writing to Rothmann.text
20 February 1592 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Christoph RothmannReproaches Rothmann for nearly eighteen months of silence since his visit to Hven, and reports learning through Rothmann's brother Johannes that he had been detained by illness.text
20 February 1592 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Moritz, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselIntroduces himself formally to Moritz, recalling a brief meeting at Kassel when Moritz was young and noting Rothmann's report that Tycho's name is already known to him.text
22 March 1592 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusSends the first printed gathering of the Progymnasmata with six extra copies for distribution, explaining that Curtius persuaded him to publish a forerunner volume of his planned astronomical restoration.text
2 April 1592 [O.S.]Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Tycho BraheThanks Tycho for elk-procurement efforts, and reports that three of four elk recently obtained from Sweden have died, possibly from eating rotten acorns after an unusually heavy mast year.text
2 April 1592 [O.S.]Moritz, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Tycho BraheDemurs at Tycho's high praise of his poetic abilities, but nonetheless sends a commendatory poem for the forthcoming Opera Astronomica as requested.text
30 July 1592 [O.S.]Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel → Tycho BraheAsks why the promised Norwegian elk have not been delivered, noting his April courier went unanswered and that his existing Swedish elk have all died.text
20 September 1592 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselExplains the delay in delivering the promised Norwegian elk, reporting that his kinsman Axel Gyldenstierne found no skipper willing to transport them safely from Norway.text
21 September 1592 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Moritz, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselThanks Moritz for composing a commendatory poem for the astronomical works and notes that the verses will stand as a lasting token of his favour.text
28 September 1592 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusReports receiving no letter from Hagecius all summer and attributes the silence to courier faithlessness rather than any failure on Hagecius's part.text
5 November 1592 [O.S.]Heinrich Brucaeus → Tycho BraheReports finding no printer's assistant via Myliander and questions how Craig can refute the parallax evidence placing the recent comet in the supralunary region.text
2 December 1592 [N.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheExplains his long silence by recounting months of serious illness: recurring stomach pain followed by jaundice and a continuous fever lasting through the summer.text
22 December 1592 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Moritz, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselReports to Moritz that the Norwegian elk repeatedly promised to his late father Wilhelm could not be delivered alive despite repeated efforts.text
9 January 1593 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Henrik RantzauAsks Rantzau to assist with forwarding perspective drawings sent by his former architect, now supervising construction of Varberg castle in Halland.text
20 April 1593 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusAcknowledges Hagecius's December letter describing his serious illnesses, expresses sympathy, and advises against strong purging medicines in favour of gentle remedies suited to old age.text
24 December 1593 [O.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheApologizes for a year of epistolary silence, attributing it to the burdens of office, poor health, and failing memory in his sixty-eighth year.text
1594 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusExpresses relief at Hagecius's survival, questions whether his earlier letter and two copies of the Progymnasmata Astronomica were received.text
28 September 1594 [O.S.]Christoph Rothmann → Tycho BraheExplains his long absence by severe arthritis and nephritic pain, reports a partial recovery, and mentions searching Frankfurt catalogues.text
23 October 1594 [O.S.]Cort Aslaksen → Tycho BraheApologizes for six months of silence due to remote location, reporting a previous letter sent via a Marburg messenger accompanying a paper-maker for Tycho's mill.text
14 January 1595 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Christoph RothmannAcknowledges Rothmann's long-awaited letter, condoles with him over prolonged illness from Tartareous salts, and resumes their suspended astronomical correspondence.text
12 August 1595 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusExpresses joy at receiving Hagecius's letter after nearly three years of silence, having feared that advancing age and illness had proved fatal.text
19 February 1596 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Cort AslaksenThanks Aslaksen for Pitiscus's book on triangles, praises it, and invites Pitiscus to correspond, expressing a wish that more clergymen possessed skill in geometry.text
22 February 1597 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Henrik RantzauThanks Rantzau for forwarding dispatches and promises regarding correction of the Spanish patent, and reports receiving a request from Archbishop Ernst of Cologne for astronomical and astrological communication.text
31 March 1597 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Henrik RantzauNotes that several letters, some for Rantzau's eyes only, have gone unanswered, and urges a reply, assuring him the matter discussed is being actively pursued.text
17 June 1597 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Moritz, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselExplains the delay in replying due to his departure from Denmark, thanks Moritz for investigating Erik Lange's financial affairs and debts, and reports currently tarrying at Rostock.text
17 September 1597 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Henrik RantzauThanks Rantzau for estates offered and requests a location near a large town where a printing-house, engravers, and instrument-makers are available to complete his books.text
13 December 1597 [O.S.]Johannes Kepler → Tycho BraheIntroduces himself to Tycho, sends the Prodromus dissertationum cosmographicarum, and requests Tycho's judgment on the work, citing Maestlin's prior approval.text
1598 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusThanks Hagecius for arranging to send a defamatory pamphlet and declines to reply to its author, deeming him unworthy of refutation.text
18 February 1598 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Anders Sørensen VedelRebukes Vedel for adopting a judge's tone and for failing to keep a promised journey, addressing also some matters concerning Lange and English letters.text
14 March 1598 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Joseph Justus ScaligerIntroduces himself to Scaliger via the bearer Frans Tengnagel, expresses long-held admiration, and praises the newly received De Temporum Emendatione.text
31 March 1598 [O.S.]Daniel Cramer → Holger RosenkrantzWarmly acknowledges two letters from Rosenkrantz expressing deep affection, though noting they were tinged with bitterness by some unhappy news they also conveyed.text
April 1598 [O.S.]Georg Rollenhagen → Tycho BraheDescribes how a kinsman at the Imperial court shared Ursus's attacking pamphlet, which was briefly lost through a friend's carelessness before being recovered.text
1 April 1598 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Johannes KeplerAcknowledges Kepler's letter and praises the Prodromus Dissertationum Cosmographicarum, admiring its wit and the ingenious speculation binding planetary distances to the regular solids.text
10 April 1598 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Anders Sørensen VedelPresses Vedel to respond about provisions to be procured for Tycho's use and to enlist friends and kinsmen in securing them.text
21 April 1598Tycho Brahe → Michael MästlinRecalls a ten-year-old promise by Maestlin to read and comment on Tycho's 1577 comet book, and reproaches him for never writing.text
24 May 1598 [O.S.]Daniel Cramer → Tycho BraheSends a promised Propempticon poem for Tycho's Urania, confirms dispatch of the testimony on the Liddelian plagiarism, and announces his doctoral promotion at Wittenberg.text
30 May 1598 [N.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheUrges Tycho to come to Prague without delay, reporting that Vice-Chancellor Coraduz has commended him favourably to the Emperor.text
18 June 1598 [O.S.]Georg Rollenhagen → Tycho BraheShares his kinsman's intelligence about Ursus and the Emperor's expectation of Tycho, and reports speaking with the Lord of Brunswick on Tycho's behalf.text
25 June 1598 [N.S.]Ernst of Bavaria, Archbishop-Elector of Cologne → Henrik RantzauExpresses keen pleasure at Brahe's work samples and Rantzau's recommendation, and promises to continue cherishing Brahe as worthy of Denmark and Germany.text
9 July 1598Joseph Justus Scaliger → Tycho BraheExpresses relief at finally learning Tycho's whereabouts after his departure from Denmark, and writes now that his location at Wandsbek is known.text
23 August 1598 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Joseph Justus ScaligerThanks Scaliger for his concern about affairs, for discussions of chronology and stellar reckoning, and for courteously receiving Tengnagel; declines to detail the reasons for his departure.text
28 November 1598 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Giovanni Antonio MaginiAcknowledges, five years after receipt, Magini's Tabula Tetragonica (dedicated to him) and notes his approval while observing that the calculations are not fully worked through.text
1 December 1598 [N.S.]Thaddaeus Hagecius → Tycho BraheForwards a note from Coraduz bearing the Emperor's resolution, received just before Hagecius's departure, and adds nothing further beyond this dispatch.text
30 December 1598 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Anders Sørensen VedelRecounts the journey from Wandsbek toward Prague, halted at Dresden when plague in Bohemia worsened and the Emperor withdrew, having been summoned through Coraduz and Hagecius.text
February 1599Johannes Kepler → Tycho BraheExplains the ten-month delay receiving Tycho's reply via Maestlin, acknowledges most excerpted words in his Ursus letters as his own, but sees no proven crime in their publication.text
26 February 1599 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Thaddaeus HageciusReports the imperial summons to Prague via Coraduz, explains delay due to deep snow and horses sold at Leipzig, and plans to depart within fourteen days.text
17 April 1599 [O.S.]Tycho Brahe → Joseph Justus ScaligerThanks Scaliger for two books sent as gifts and for excerpting, in his own hand, the key passages from Hipparchus and Ptolemy on the fixed stars.text
23 July 1599 [N.S.]Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg → Tycho BraheCongratulates Tycho on his imperial summons to Prague, expresses confidence the Emperor will retain him there, and offers assistance with Tycho's studies.text
31 August 1599 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Johann Georg Herwart von HohenburgReports his establishment at Benátky castle under imperial patronage and plans to pursue astronomical and alchemical work there, with instruments being transferred from Magdeburg.text
17 September 1599 [N.S.]Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg → Tycho BraheAcknowledges receipt of Tycho's lunar eclipse calculation, congratulates him on imperial patronage, and discusses whether the star of Mercury can eclipse Venus.text
18 September 1599 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Anders Sørensen VedelNarrates the circumstances of his departure from Denmark, recounting his warning to the King's Chancellor about the threatened fate of his observatory at Uraniborg.text
26 September 1599 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Daniel CramerRefers Cramer to an enclosed copy of his letter to Holger Rosenkrantz for news of his situation, requesting confidentiality, and hints at a separate matter personally concerning Cramer.text
4 November 1599 [N.S.]Giovanni Antonio Magini → Tycho BraheReports Tengnagel's Carnival visit delivering Tycho's letter and the Mechanica, explains why Tengnagel could not convey the secret commission, and accounts for the ensuing delay in replying.text
16 November 1599 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Johann Georg Herwart von HohenburgAcknowledges receipt of two letters and the Bavarian library catalogue, explaining his delayed reply by his busy correspondence while sending his eldest son to retrieve instruments from Magdeburg.text
9 December 1599 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Johannes KeplerApologizes for delayed reply, excuses Kepler regarding Ursus's insertion of his letter, and describes the disruption caused by relocating his affairs to Bohemia.text
31 December 1599 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Johann Georg Herwart von HohenburgReports receiving Herwart's latest brief letter just before the winter solstice and thanks him for patience with delayed replies and continued friendship.text
3 January 1600 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Giovanni Antonio MaginiAcknowledges Magini's letters via Tengnagel, encloses a brief account of his departure from Denmark and added verses, and urges prompt completion of a promised task.text
26 January 1600 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Johannes KeplerReports receiving Kepler's letter and urges him to travel at once to Benátky, noting a previous reply was sent via Blotius in Vienna.text
2 March 1600 [O.S.]Wolfgang Franzius → Tycho BraheReports that the runaway Transylvanian has asked forgiveness, wishes Tycho good health after plague in Bohemia, and hopes theological disputes have subsided.text
4 March 1600 [N.S.]Giovanni Antonio Magini → Tycho BraheAcknowledges a confidential commission, reports arranging the translation of some eight German letters into Latin, and discusses assistance from a Transylvanian student.text
10 March 1600 [N.S.]Joseph Justus Scaliger → Tycho BraheExplains his failure to locate Tycho after Wittenberg, describes false reports that Tycho had settled in Silesia, and mentions Longomontanus as his informant.text
27 March 1600 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Wolfgang FranziusReports that the epidemic has subsided and the Emperor lingers at Pilsen but is expected soon in Prague, and discusses an untrustworthy Transylvanian who had sought his letters.text
April 1600 [N.S.]Johannes Kepler → Tycho BraheApologises for his recent intemperance during his stay at Benátky, recounting Tycho's liberal hospitality and shared observations, and expressing remorse for his conduct.text
1 April 1600 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Daniel CramerThanks Cramer for an ode to the Emperor and pledges to support his bid for the imperial laurel, noting the Emperor's absence from Prague due to plague in Bohemia.text
3 April 1600 [N.S.]Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg → Tycho BraheSends Frankfurt spring fair book catalogues and several books, including works by Gemma Frisius, Camerarius, Peurbach emended by Orontius Finaeus, and the Tables of Queen Elizabeth of England.text
5 April 1600 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Georg RollenhagenReports having assisted a Hamburg citizen through court intermediaries at Rollenhagen's request, and says no further solicitation of the Senate is needed since the Emperor has intervened directly.text
5 April 1600 [N.S.]Johannes Kepler → Tycho BraheFormally acknowledges his arrival at Benátky on 4 February 1600, Tycho's hospitality, and the sharing of observations and astronomical labours, committing to confidentiality regarding the material shared.text
11 April 1600 [N.S.]Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg → Tycho BraheWarns of postal negligence in Prague and asks Tycho to route future letters through Alexander Prandtl or Johann Menhard rather than the postmaster, to ensure reliable delivery.text
17 April 1600 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Susanne HájekPromises to write to his Lübeck factor to pursue Susanne's debtor David Heidler on her behalf, and asks for news of her husband Dr. Thaddaeus Hájek's health.text
18 April 1600 [N.S.]Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg → Tycho BraheSends several books Tycho requested, including the Prutenic Tables and Copernicus On Triangles, and reports manuscript exemplars of Hipparchus and Ptolemy's Great Syntaxis available for collation.text
26 April 1600 [N.S.]Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg → Tycho BraheSends two books by François Viète and reports plans to travel to Augsburg to seek out posthumous manuscript works of Cyprian Leovitius and transmit them to Tycho.text
4 May 1600 [N.S.]Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg → Tycho BraheAcknowledges receipt of Tycho's April letter, expresses relief that none of their letters have been lost, and anticipates receiving Tycho's revised lunar hypothesis.text
8 May 1600 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Georg von WolframsdorfReports his prosperous condition in Bohemia under imperial protection and offers assistance at the imperial court, directing Wolframsdorf to Jessenius for fuller particulars.text
June 1600Tycho Brahe → Johannes KeplerCertifies that Kepler spent four months (February–May 1600) at Benátky working diligently on astronomical exercises with Tycho's instruments and observations.text
19 June 1600 [O.S.]Georg Rollenhagen → Tycho BraheReports that the Magdeburg canons are ready to purchase Tycho's astronomical equipment and that two boatmen offer to ship it to Leitmeritz, pressing for a reply.text
23 July 1600 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Joseph Justus ScaligerThanks Scaliger for his March letter, reports being summoned to Prague by Emperor Rudolf II, and mentions a chance meeting with Nicolaus Suckerback of Meissen, newly arrived from Italy.text
28 August 1600 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Johannes KeplerExplains the delay in reply, reports being summoned from Benátky to Prague for a private audience with Emperor Rudolf II, and begins narrating what has since transpired.text
28 August 1600 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Johann Georg Herwart von HohenburgApologizes for infrequent replies to Herwart's many letters, explains the delay by work on the restitution of the lunar hypothesis, and promises to address Herwart's doubts.text
8 September 1600 [N.S.]Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg → Tycho BraheRecounts earlier failed efforts to obtain a laudatory poem from Philipp Menzel in Tycho's honour, and announces that he has now succeeded in procuring one, sent herewith.text
11 September 1600 [N.S.]Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg → Tycho BraheReports delivering the Mechanica to Philipp Eduard Fugger at Augsburg and transmits Kepler's earlier letter on Tycho's hypotheses, noting that Ursus, who arrogated them, is now dead.text
23 September 1600 [N.S.]Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg → Tycho BraheSends two books Tycho requested: the Works of Apollonius of Perga and the astronomical tables of Blanchinus, Prugner, and Peurbach.text
26 September 1600 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Georg RollenhagenReports his goods arrived in Bohemia and asks Rollenhagen to deliver the enclosed letter to the Dean, explaining that the earlier silence was due to pressing imperial duties.text
17 October 1600Johannes Kepler → Tycho BraheSets out the terms of their contract — two years of astronomical assistance with Imperial backing — and reviews grievances arising from his current situation in Bohemia.text
8 November 1600 [N.S.]Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg → Tycho BraheReports finding errors in his own calculations from Tycho's worked examples and marvels that Tycho's eclipse calculation of 10 July agrees with observation to within one arc-minute.text
10 November 1600 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Moritz, Landgrave of Hesse-KasselUses Bopenhausen's return to greet the Landgrave, acknowledges the late Landgrave Wilhelm's past favour, and affirms his continued wish to be of service to Hesse-Kassel.text
16 November 1600 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Christoph SturtzDiscusses Swedish and Livonian affairs and leaves to Sturtz's judgement what the late Chytraeus wished inserted in the Historiola, with Gödelmann carrying the relevant documents.text
27 November 1600 [N.S.]Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg → Tycho BraheReports that Warszewicki did not arrive, expresses concern for Kepler's lack of a secure position, promises to seek astronomical tables, and sends works by Angelus.text
10 December 1600 [N.S.]Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg → Tycho BraheSends the Alphonsine Tables and a transcription of Methodius's Revelation, expressing admiration for Tycho's new solar and lunar calculation.text
24 January 1601 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Giovanni Antonio MaginiWrites via his son accompanying Anthony Sherley's Persian legation to Rome, thanks Magini for handling a confidential commission, and discusses Baldi of Urbino's proposed writing project.text
20 February 1601 [N.S.]Giovanni Antonio Magini → Tycho BraheExplains delay in carrying out Tycho's undisclosed commission, citing reliance on third parties such as Sagredo and the press of domestic obligations.text
10 March 1601 [O.S.]Christoph Sturtz → Tycho BraheReports Duke Charles's occupation of almost all Livonia, the Polish Diet's resolution to wage war for three years, and personal losses from these events.text
15 April 1601 [N.S.]Tycho Brahe → Christoph SturtzThanks Sturtz for writing and reports political and military news: the Wallachian's new vassal status under the Emperor, Báthory's invasion of Transylvania, and preparations for the renewed Hungarian war.text
18 April 1601 [O.S.]Georg Rollenhagen → Tycho BraheReports forwarding Petkum's reply via a student carrier, notes furnaces from Hamburg delayed by Elbe flooding, and encloses a prognostication on the Turkish war by Dethard Horst.text
15 May 1601Georg Rollenhagen → Tycho BraheDescribes David Fabricius's visit and his observations, laments Fabricius's pastoral constraints, and reports the Bishop of Cologne's mission to the Emperor concerning election of a King of the Romans.text

The printed works themselves: Typographica.

10The translations and their checking

How the English was made and how far it has been checked. The translations were produced in 2026 by a large language model working from the transcribed originals, each with a self-assessment of its own reliability. An independent pass then read every translation against the original and, for 457 of the 508 documents, against the page images of Dreyer’s edition; that pass logged 289 defects, most of them in the transcribed Latin rather than in the English, and they were corrected. Its paragraph on each letter — which pages were read, what was found, what remains doubtful — is the warrant printed beneath the translation, and its grade is the one shown; the self-assessment is kept in the dataset but not printed, because its grade was revised on 214 documents and a reader should see one judgement, not two. An uncollated translation is graded at most Probable, whatever the checker thought of it. No human Latinist has reviewed any translation; a sampled review of the non-Secure letters is a desideratum (§11).

The grades as applied

GradeMeaningDocuments
Athe check against Dreyer's page images found no defect in the English; the translation may be quoted for sense, the original for words454
Bsound in sense, with soft points the warrant names, or not collated against Dreyer's pages (the cap)52
Csubstantive uncertainties remain; the warrant names them2

Conventions of the texts

The original is printed with tekstnet's ligatures (æ, œ) and the edition's paragraphing; where the two transcriptions of tekstnet's page disagree in a word the letter page lists both readings under the original. The English is printed without the translator's emphasis; its bracketed words are the translator's supplements and its bracketed queries the translator's doubts, both left as they stand. Greek is printed as the edition gives it.

11Desiderata

What this edition does not have, does not know, or has not yet checked — with the count, the documents or repositories concerned, and what would settle each item. A reader who can supply any of it is asked to write to the editor.

  1. Letters published since Dreyer and absent from the edition — 7 items, listed with print and archive; settled by editing them as a separately keyed addendum once Christianson 1972 has been obtained and the DSL has been asked whether it will add them.

  2. Correspondences known to be lost — from Norlind 1970:
    • No letter survives from 1569 or 1570 (Norlind 1970, p. 174).
    • Tycho's letters to Anders Sørensen Vedel, some fifty of them, burned with Bishop Christen Worm's library in the Copenhagen fire of 1728; Vedel's letters to Tycho are lost (Norlind 1970, pp. 174–175).
    • Holger Rosenkrantz's papers burned at Fredrikshald in 1826; his exchange with Tycho survives only in Jacob Langebek's eighteenth-century transcripts, now in Rigsarkivet (Norlind 1970, pp. 173–174).
    • Letters to and from Tycho are known to lie unpublished in the Herwart and Rosenkrantz papers (Norlind 1970, p. 176).
  3. Translations not collated against Dreyer's pages — 51 documents (§10), 47 of them in vol. VI, which tekstnet does not paginate; the pages have since been located by search (§6) and the collation can now be run. Settled by running it.
  4. No human review of the English — all 508 translations are machine-made and machine-checked. Settled by a Latinist's sampled review, beginning with the 54 not graded Secure.
  5. Words where the two transcriptions of tekstnet's text disagree — 80 documents, 1664 words in all, listed on each letter page; settled word by word against Dreyer's page.
  6. Witnessed documents without a record-level catalogue link — 336 of 439; the repository table (§5) says what exists online. Basel first: e-manuscripta lists item-level digitisations under G I 35 and G I 23, to be matched by shelfmark and folio.

  7. The Marburg convolute — HStAM Best. 3 II Nr. 1070 holds originals of the Hven–Kassel exchange of 1585–1592; which letters it holds has not been read letter by letter from the Arcinsys images, so no record cites it as a witness. Settled by reading them.
  8. The unmarked witness lines — 236 of 475 lines say nothing about what the manuscript is; most Vienna and Basel lines are originals or drafts, but the edition does not say so and the repository catalogues have not been checked line by line.
  9. The press flag — 218 documents are flagged as concerning Tycho's printed books by the editor's reading, with no per-letter work recorded; settled by recording the work (and its Typographica entry) on each.
  10. Places not keyed to Loca — 36 of 61 places of writing are not in Tycho's own gazetteer, because he was never there; they are located here from the edition's datelines with coordinates of the modern town.
  11. A record-level concordance to Early Modern Letters Online — EMLO catalogues the same printed corpus as 505 letters; the two have not been matched record by record.
  12. The right to republish tekstnet's texts — the terms under which the DSL's texts stand here beside an English translation are to be stated in §12 once the DSL has been asked.

The repositories

Catalogue links and digitisation statements for every holding institution are in the repository table (§5); each was checked on the edition date or is marked as reported and not verified.

How to cite this edition. Westergaard, C., “Epistolarium — The Letters of Tycho Brahe”, Tychoniana, edition of 5 September 2026, §n, record key. Example: §3, brahe-t_15881013001; the letter itself as letters/brahe-t_15881013001.html. The dataset is data.json; the catalogue letters.csv; the texts in one file all.html.
